1.explanation: Prism’s definitions for C and its base 'clike' language contain the regex that matches numeric literals. In components/prism-c.js (and its minified counterpart) the 'number' pattern is missing support for single-quote separators. Since Prism.languages.c extends clike and overrides number, updating prism-c.js (and regenerating prism-c.min.js) to include ' in the digit patterns is required. If you prefer a broader change for all 'clike' languages, you would also update the 'number' regex in components/prism-clike.js to accept ' as a digit separator.
1.bug_scenario: In C++ numeric literals (both integer and floating-point) the single quote (') can be used as a separator (e.g. 1'000'000, 1.23'45e-6), but Prism’s C/C++ highlighter treats the quote as a string delimiter and breaks the literal into a string token. The screenshots show Prism highlighting everything after the first quote as a string (red), whereas the entire token should be highlighted as a number (yellow).
